documents.title: Oncology staging summary and treatment plan
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/08/2024

Re: Philip Hickey, 57

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the right lower lobe of the lung, mediastinal nodal involvement on EBUS (12/19/2023).

Staging:
- PET-CT 01/03/2024: FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and FDG-avid mediastinal nodes. No FDG-avid disease outside the chest.
- MRI brain with and without contrast 01/04/2024: no intracranial metastatic disease.
- Molecular profiling of the tumor: no EGFR mutation, no ALK rearrangement.
Clinical stage IIIB. Reviewed at our thoracic tumor board: not a surgical candidate given the nodal disease; recommendation is definitive concurrent chemoradiation.

Plan: weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel given with thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, start 01/22/2024. Radiation oncology simulation done 01/10. Weekly labs during treatment. We discussed goals - treatment is given with curative intent.

We strongly encouraged him to stop smoking; he is not ready to commit.
Medications: psyllium, ibuprofen PRN, albuterol PRN, polyethylene glycol PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Hematology & Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to check in before chemoradiation starts on the 22nd. Staging done - stage IIIB adenocarcinoma RLL, no spread outside the chest on PET, brain MRI clear, no EGFR/ALK. Plan is weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel with 6 weeks of radiation, curative intent. He has met radiation oncology.

How he's doing: sleeping a little better since he has a plan. Breathing about the same as November. Cough, occasional blood streaks, no big bleeds. Appetite fair.
Smoking: still about 1.5 ppd. We talked about how stopping now could help him get through radiation. Offered varenicline, nicotine replacement, or a referral to the cancer center's tobacco program. He says he can't take on one more thing this month. Will ask again.

Vitals reviewed, weight stable since oncology visit. Lungs: no wheeze, no increased work of breathing. Heart regular.

A/P:
- Lung adenocarcinoma, stage IIIB - treatment per oncology. Asked him to keep us posted, and to message for anything non-cancer.
- Constipation - chemo antiemetics can make it worse; keep fiber going and use MiraLAX daily if needed.
- Knees - ibuprofen sparingly during chemo; check with oncology about using it.
- Tobacco - declines a medication today.
RTC 2 months or sooner.

documents.title: Bowels
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Halfway through the radiation. Bowels are slow again, 4 days no BM. Can I take more of the MiraLAX

documents.title: RE: Bowels
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Hickey, yes - you can take the MiraLAX every day, even twice a day for a day or two until things move, then back to once daily. Keep up the fluids and the Metamucil. If you have belly pain, vomiting, or still nothing after 2 more days, call us or your oncology team.

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY END-OF-TREATMENT SUMMARY
Patient: Philip Hickey
Diagnosis: right lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma, stage IIIB
Course: thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 01/22/2024 through 03/01/2024, with weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel given by medical oncology. All fractions delivered, no treatment breaks.
Tolerance: fatigue, expected.
Follow-up: restaging CT chest in about 5 weeks with medical oncology; radiation oncology visit in 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from home. Finished chemoradiation 3/1, all 30 treatments. Tired, napping in the afternoons, slowly getting more energy. Eating better than in February. Cough a little less. Bowels OK on daily MiraLAX + fiber.
Smoking: still smoking daily. Not ready for a med.
Restaging CT with oncology early April.
A/P: recovering from chemoradiation. Continue current meds. Will see him after oncology restaging.

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST
Comparison: 12/11/2023.
Findings: Right lower lobe mass now 2.6 cm (previously 4.0 cm). Mediastinal nodes decreased in size. No new pulmonary nodule. No pleural effusion. Mild post-radiation change in the right lower lobe and right paramediastinal lung within the treatment field. No new osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Treatment response: right lower lobe mass decreased to 2.6 cm. No new disease.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/17/2024  Discharged: 05/21/2024
Service: Hematology/Oncology

Principal problem: symptomatic anemia during chemotherapy, complicated by transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI).

History: 57-year-old man with stage IIIB right lower lobe adenocarcinoma diagnosed in December, treated with concurrent chemoradiation and now on consolidation carboplatin/paclitaxel (cycle 2 on 05/06). About a month of increasing fatigue and shortness of breath. Takes ibuprofen chronically for knee osteoarthritis. Known iron deficiency anemia. Admitted for evaluation of worsening anemia.

Course: Hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL with MCV 78 fL on arrival. Given IV fluids, then started on packed red blood cells. About 2 hours into the transfusion he developed chills and discomfort. T 38.5 C, HR 102, BP 124/78, SpO2 98% on room air. At that point he denied back pain, dark urine, rash or trouble breathing. Exam: pale conjunctivae, mild tachycardia. Transfusion was stopped and the blood bank notified; direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test negative.
Over the next two hours his oxygen saturation fell to 86% on room air with respiratory rate 28. Portable chest film showed new bilateral infiltrates; NT-proBNP 180 pg/mL, no clinical volume overload. Diagnosed with TRALI and reported to the blood bank. Supported with nasal cannula oxygen up to 5 L/min; he did not need intubation. Weaned to room air by 05/19. Repeat film 05/20 showed the infiltrates clearing.
Anemia: ferritin 6 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 4% - iron deficiency, most likely from chronic NSAID use, with chemotherapy contributing. Ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV given 05/20; second 750 mg dose scheduled at the infusion center 05/28. Ibuprofen stopped. Hemoglobin 7.9 at discharge.

Discharge medications: psyllium daily; albuterol HFA PRN; polyethylene glycol 3350 PRN. STOP ibuprofen.
Allergies: NKDA. Add to record: history of TRALI - transfusion medicine consult before any future transfusion.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; oncology 06/10. No further chemotherapy cycles planned at this time.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for knee pain. Max 3,000 mg per day.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital 5/17-5/21 for anemia (Hgb 7.4) on consolidation chemo. Reaction to the blood transfusion with fever then low oxygen and bilateral infiltrates - TRALI. Needed oxygen for 2 days, no ICU, no intubation. IV iron in the hospital, second dose at the infusion center this morning. Discharge summary reviewed and meds reconciled.

Today: breathing back to his usual. No fever. Still tired. Knees are bothering him off the ibuprofen.

Vitals reviewed, SpO2 normal on RA. Wt 86 kg. Pale but less so per him. Lungs: no crackles, no wheeze. Heart regular, no edema.
CBC in clinic: Hgb 9.4 - up from 7.9 at discharge.

A/P:
1. TRALI - resolved clinically. Added to his record; any future transfusion needs a transfusion medicine review first.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - improving with IV iron. Recheck CBC and iron in 6-8 weeks.
3. Knee OA - no more ibuprofen or other NSAIDs. Start acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 every 6 hours as needed, no more than 3 g a day. Ice, and we can revisit an injection when he's further from chemo.
4. Lung cancer - oncology 6/10 to decide next steps.
5. Tobacco - still smoking. Offered help again; not yet.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 06/10/2024

Stage IIIB RLL adenocarcinoma, s/p concurrent chemoradiation (completed 03/01/2024) and two consolidation cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel. Admission in May for anemia complicated by TRALI; recovered.
We discussed consolidation durvalumab. Given the recent lung injury and the risk of immune pneumonitis in the treated lung, we have elected not to start it. He agrees.
Treatment is complete. Surveillance: CT chest every 3-4 months for 2 years, then less often. Next CT in August.
Anemia improving on IV iron. Off NSAIDs.
Allergies: NKDA. History of TRALI.
Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Blood count and iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news - your hemoglobin is up to 12.5 and your iron stores are refilled after the IV iron. No more iron needed right now. Stay off the ibuprofen and we'll recheck at your physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
58M, annual exam.

Interval: stage IIIB RLL adenocarcinoma, chemoradiation Jan-Mar, 2 consolidation cycles, admission in May for anemia with TRALI. Treatment done, surveillance CTs with oncology; August CT showed further shrinkage, nothing new.
Feels well. Appetite good, weight coming back (91 kg). Cough at baseline. No hemoptysis since spring. Knees manageable with acetaminophen; has not been taking ibuprofen. Bowels OK with fiber, MiraLAX now and then.
Smoking: still daily, about the same amount. He knows. Said he'd think about varenicline after the holidays.
Alcohol: a couple beers on weekends.

Meds: psyllium daily, acetaminophen PRN, albuterol PRN, PEG PRN.
Allergies: NKDA. History of TRALI (transfusion).

Exam: Well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs without wheeze or crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft, NT. Knees no effusion. Ext no edema. Skin intact.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2021 normal, next 2031. Tdap 2022. PCV20 done. Shingrix complete. Flu + COVID next month at nurse visit. HCV/HIV done 2022.
- Labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c.
- Lung cancer - surveillance with oncology.
- IDA - recheck Hgb today; avoid NSAIDs.
- Tobacco - 2 minutes on cessation; not ready, open to revisiting in January.
RTC 4-5 months.
